subject: Dedicated Capacity — Discovery recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated Capacity — Discovery recap & next steps

Hi Sophia / Rajesh —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our call and the proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. Please reply with any corrections or add anything I missed.

Summary of your goals / pain points
- Predictable throughput for inference spikes (billing-sensitive trading alerts workload with daily peaks at 9:30am ET). Current infra struggles to hit consistent TPS during market open.
- Data isolation and compliance: need per-tenant isolation and the ability to run in a VPC with restricted egress.
- Lower per-token cost vs spot-managed serving; hoping to reduce inference cost by ~30% vs current Kubernetes-based GPU autoscaling.
- Strict SLA requirement for core models (p99 latency target ~120ms for short prompts).

Current stack and constraints
- Models: mix of Llama-2 13B (quantized) and a homegrown reranker; deployed on EKS with GPU nodes.
- Peak inference demand: ~1.5k TPS short spikes; sustained baseline 200–300 TPS.
- Data residency: primary in us-west-2; security team requires SOC2 evidence and KMS integration.

Success criteria for a Dedicated fit
1) Reserved GPU pool that delivers predictable TPS for market-open spikes (support for reserved capacity + burst policy).
2) Network isolation (VPC peering / private control plane) and KMS/HSM integration.
3) Autoscaling rules that allow predictable burst from reserved baseline to N extra GPUs for X minutes without affecting p99 SLA.
4) Cost target: ~30% unit-cost reduction compared to current setup, or clear plan to hit that post-quantization tuning.
5) A short pilot (2–4 weeks) for validating latency and throughput with shadow traffic and a small subset of users.

Proposed next steps / mutual action plan
- Redwood: share Dedicated capacity overview + pilot T&Cs (attached: redwood-dedicated-overview.pdf).
- FinSolve: share current workload replay (samples + traffic profile) and confirm compliance docs to expedite SOC2/KMS review — suggested files: finsolve-current-arch.png and the AWS billing/usage for the last 30 days.
- Schedule technical deep-dive with Aditya (SE) to go over autoscaling/burst thresholds and kernel/quantization tuning: proposed slot Thurs 2/19 10:00am PT.
- If pilot looks good, align on contract terms and reserved capacity commitment (Rafael will lead commercial).

Notes re: Dedicated specifics we discussed
- Reserved GPU pools: we can reserve a baseline capacity for your 300 TPS sustained and configure a burst pool to add GPUs for short spikes; bursts are billed differently and can be capped.
- Autoscaling policy: support scheduled and traffic-driven scaling. We can create a policy that adds N GPUs when queue latency > 50ms for > 30s, with a max burst duration (e.g., 20 minutes) to control spend.
- Isolation: private control plane + VPC peering and customer-managed KMS keys are supported.

Please confirm the proposed Thurs deep-dive or share times that work for you.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated Capacity — Discovery recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and captures the discussion well. A few clarifications/requests from our side: 

1) Burst behavior: when you say "burst pool" — can you confirm if a burst GPU adds are pre-warmed (i.e., cold start time) or if there's a warm buffer? Our market-open spikes are short (~8–12 minutes) so startup time matters.

2) Autoscaling policy: we like the rule you suggested. Can Aditya share recommended thresholds for Llama-2 13B quantized so we can compare to our telemetry?

3) Security docs: we'll share SOC2 in progress and want to see the KMS integration flow (diagram preferred). Can you attach the SOC2 evidence template you referenced?

4) Pilot scope: prefer a 3-week pilot with shadow traffic plus a 1-hour canary test for customers. For billing, we need clarity whether pilot burst usage will be charged at the burst rate or covered as part of the evaluation credits.

We're good for the technical deep-dive on Thurs 2/19 10:00am PT. Rajesh (CTO) will join.

Best,
Sophia
Head of Platform Engineering | FinSolve
Sophia.Li@finsolve.com

Thanks — confirmed for Thurs 2/19 10:00am PT (Zoom link below). Reply-all if anything changes.

Addressing your questions quickly:
- Burst pre-warming: we support a configurable warm buffer. For workloads like yours (8–12min spikes) we recommend keeping 1–2 GPUs pre-warmed in the burst pool to avoid cold-start penalties; we’ll run the replay during the pilot to validate.
- Aditya will bring recommended thresholds and kernel/quantization tuning notes to the deep-dive. He’ll also run a short load-profile against a similar model config during the pilot to validate p99.
- Security: attaching the SOC2 evidence template and a short KMS integration diagram (we’ll upload to the Drive folder and share).
- Pilot billing: Redwood can cover up to 20 GPU-hours of burst during the evaluation as credits; anything above will be billed at the burst rate. We'll formalize this in the MA/Quote.
